newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. contractor pays $22.8 mln to settle claim.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. contractor pays $22.8 mln to settle claim.

text.p: A contractor will pay the U.S. government $22.8 million to settle claims it overcharged the Veterans Affairs Department for medical equipment, the Justice Department announced Thursday.

Olympus America Inc., of Melville, New York, agreed to the settlement after an investigation showed the company overcharged Veterans Affairs by not giving it the same discount as it offered to commercial customers, the department said.

"When companies do business with the government and promise to give the government a fair price, we intend to hold them to their bargain," Assistant Attorney General Frank Hunger said in a written statement.

Hunger said Olympus' contracting personnel failed to provide Veterans Affairs negotiators with accurate information about its commercial pricing practices for such equipment as colonscopes, laparascopes and other medical supplies.
Olympus offered private businesss a discount on the equipment but offered a smaller discount to the government, he said.
